brief: Citadel Securities (Nohshad Shah) reiterates last week's bullish equity call into the midterms, citing stronger AI fundamentals and the prospect of greater stability in long-end yields. This week's market rebound, led by AI-related technology, has started moving in that direction. The note argues compute demand is unevenly distributed: OpenAI's top-decile enterprise customers now generate 8.3x as many output tokens per active user as median firms, up from 2.6x in January, while independent survey data show only 45% of workers use generative AI, 14% daily, touching just 6% of work hours, leaving an enormous diffusion runway across almost 900mn knowledge workers globally. GPT-6 Astra's significance is shifting AI from answering questions to completing longer, multi-step work. Under a Jevons paradox dynamic, cheaper and more capable AI expands the number of economically viable tasks faster than efficiency reduces compute per task, so total compute consumption rises rather than falls. This demand is colliding with a constrained supply system. The author argues the more immediate risk is not overbuilding but that already-planned capacity gets absorbed before political delays, grid constraints and permitting catch up, worsened by weak public messaging on AI's benefits against China's more urgent, coordinated push.
